overview: The Council approved a new full-time substance abuse outreach position and established a pay grade for police recruits. The body also heard a major presentation on a regional transmission line project and discussed performance issues regarding the city's private parking enforcement contractor.

items.title: Public Hearing: Class 4 License
items.summary: Approved a Class 4 license for Incident Clear LLC, doing business as Medford Truck and Auto Repair, at 11 Hall Street.

items.title: Eversource Transmission Line Presentation
items.summary: Received a presentation from Eversource regarding the Mystic-to-Woburn 115 kilovolt underground transmission line project spanning 3.2 miles in Medford. The project is anticipated to begin construction in early 2017 following a Department of Public Utilities review process.

items.title: Substance Abuse Outreach Agent Position
items.summary: Approved the first reading of an ordinance adding the position of Outreach Agent Substance Abuse to the municipal compensation plan. Councilors requested a formal job description and a plan for a dedicated confidential office space within City Hall.

items.title: Library and Traffic Supervisor Compensation
items.summary: Approved compensation plan amendments for library staff and school traffic patrol supervisors, providing for 2% annual wage increases through 2018. The adjustments follow recently negotiated collective bargaining agreements.

items.title: Police Student Officer Classification
items.summary: Approved an ordinance creating a 'Student Officer' classification for candidates attending the police academy with a starting salary of $40,000. Police Chief Leo Sacco explained the classification ensures recruits do not exercise police powers before successfully completing the 800-hour state-mandated curriculum.

items.title: Republic Parking Ticket Actions
items.summary: Discussed several complaints regarding inaccurate ticketing by Republic Parking, including instances of tickets being issued before meter expiration. Police Chief Leo Sacco addressed concerns regarding kiosk accuracy and the lack of weekend office hours for appeals.

items.title: Harvard Street Zoning Appeal
items.summary: Referred a discussion regarding a proposed five-family conversion at 198-202 Harvard Street to the zoning subcommittee. The council also requested data from the Board of Appeals regarding all multi-unit conversions approved over the last ten years.

items.title: Winthrop Street Construction Debris
items.summary: Approved a resolution requesting that contractors working on Winthrop Street remove all construction equipment and debris from traffic lanes at the end of each workday.

items.title: Consolidated Information and Budget Requests
items.summary: Approved several resolutions requesting lists of prior budget appropriations, an audit of vacant board positions, and an information session for boat owners regarding Craddock Bridge waterway restrictions.

items.title: Lawrence Memorial Hospital Future
items.summary: Tabled a discussion regarding the future of Lawrence Memorial Hospital until the following week.

items.title: Routine Condolences and Fire Department Retirements
items.summary: Approved several ceremonial resolutions offering condolences to families of notable residents and congratulating four members of the Medford Fire Department on their retirements.
